To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EMC effect can be understood by considering the effects of Fermi motion, binding energy, and a reasonable ansatz for the nucleon structure functions as a function of the invariant mass of the nucleon, and that the data can be explained with a single set of parameters.

the nuclear structure functions can be explained by Fermi motion and the mass dependence of the nucleons structure function, and that this explanation is closely related to the earlier explanations based on virtual pions in nuclei.

the EMC effect can be understood as the combined effect of (a) the Fermi motion of nucleons in the nucleus and (b) a dependence of the nucleonic parton distribution function on the invariant mass of the parton.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of nucleons inside nuclei.
the structure of nuclei and their constituents, the nucleons, and the elementary particles that make up the nucleons.
the effects of the nuclear binding on the structure functions of the nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EMC effect is due to a combination of nuclear binding, Fermi motion, and a modification of the structure functions at large x and large Q2.
the EMC effect is a manifestation of the strong interaction, and that the nuclear structure functions are a measure of the nuclear wave functions.
the nuclear structure functions, as well as the nuclear binding energies, can be explained by the same mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fermi motion and binding effects can explain the nuclear structure function data, but that the data are not inconsistent with a small nuclear modification of the nucleon quark distribution function.
Fermi motion is a major factor in understanding the EMC effect, and that a simple ansatz can explain the nuclear structure function data.
the nuclear structure function is determined by the nucleon structure functions and the Fermi motion of the nucleon, and that the nuclear structure functions are consistent with the EMC effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear structure functions are determined by the structure function of the nucleon and the nuclear wave function.
Fermi motion alone can explain most of the data on nuclear structure functions.
conventional nuclear binding effects can explain much of the observed nuclear structure function behavior, and that the EMC-like effects are not necessary to explain the data.
